records.name: Feed to TAN Production

simulation_use.implementation_note: Convert PTAN mass to concentration with system water volume and removal terms.

notes: Alternative TAN-from-feed rules should remain cross-checks only.

records.name: Nitrification Oxygen and Alkalinity Demand
notes: Use these as stoichiometric demand anchors driven by TAN-N oxidation.

records.name: Biofilter Feed Loading Capacity Anchors
notes: Use feed-loading ranges as sizing anchors rather than exact guarantees.

records.name: Biofilter Startup and Maturation Dynamics

simulation_use.implementation_note: Treat startup as a lagged increase in nitrification capacity influenced by pH, DO, alkalinity, and temperature.

notes: Do not model startup as instant full nitrification capacity.

records.name: Surface-Based Biofilm Nitrification Capacity
records.equation_text: removal_g_tan_day = capacity_g_tan_day * f_concentration * f_pH * f_temperature * f_DO * biofilter_maturity; capacity_g_tan_day = sum(surface_feed_capacity_g_feed_day * tan_per_g_feed); f_concentration = min(1, TAN_mg_L / tan_saturation_mg_L)

capacity_anchors.unit: g feed / m2 raft grow area / day
capacity_anchors.source: Rakocy, Masser, Losordo, SRAC 454 'Recirculating Aquaculture Tank Production Systems: Aquaponics - Integrating Fish and Plant Culture'
capacity_anchors.quote: The waste treatment capacity of raft hydroponics is equivalent to a feeding ratio of 180 grams of fish feed
notes: Capacity equivalence, not the operating design ratio (60 to 100 g/m2/day, design 80).
SRAC 454: 'A significant amount of nitrification occurs on the undersides of the polystyrene sheets'.
Applies only when solids are removed before the raft. NFT has much smaller surface and may need a separate biofilter; no NFT capacity value is given, so NFT gets none here.

evidence_assessment.confidence_reason: University extension fact sheet by the UVI system's lead researcher, direct number. Context partial: it does not say at what TAN level the capacity applies, or whether it counts plant ammonium uptake as well as nitrification.
evidence_assessment.cross_check: Consistent with UVI's statement (Biofilters corroboration report) that the raft gives adequate biofiltration at the design feeding ratio, and with SRAC 454's note that ammonia need not be monitored after the first month. Per-m2 biofilm rates from trickling filters and RBCs (0.24 to 0.53 g TAN/m2/day) are about 10x lower per m2 of grow area, but are not directly comparable (see cross_check_note).

notes: Reuses the existing canonical media feed-loading ranges. The simulation uses the conservative low end of each range unless the scenario names a value.

evidence_assessment.inherits: biofilter_feed_loading_capacities (existing draft canon, distilled pack / SRAC 0453)
evidence_assessment.confidence_reason: Existing canonical draft values; low end used for conservatism.

concentration_response.simulation_default_basis: Upper end of the sourced 3 to 4 mg/L saturation band; the conservative choice because it gives slower removal at a given TAN.
concentration_response.source: Losordo, DeLong, Guerdat, 'TAN, other water quality factors affect nitrification rates in biofilters', Global Aquaculture Advocate, 2 May 2015 (from New Technologies in Aquaculture, ch. 31, 2009)
quotes: At these levels, there is generally a linear relationship between the TAN conversion rate and TAN concentration in the filter.
When values rise much above 3-4 mg TAN/L, there is usually no further increase in the rate of nitrification.
concentration_response.assumption: The raft capacity equivalence is treated as the saturated (maximum) rate. SRAC 454 does not state the TAN level at which it applies.

evidence_assessment.confidence_reason: Industry magazine article, though written by recognised RAS engineers (Losordo is a co-author of SRAC 454) and drawn from a published textbook chapter. Generic RAS biofilters, not aquaponic raft. Low until the textbook chapter or a peer-reviewed half-saturation constant is checked.
evidence_assessment.cross_check: Qualitatively consistent with the Chen, Ling, Blancheton 2006 review (Aquacultural Engineering 34:179-197), which names substrate concentration as a governing factor; its abstract gives no number.

pH_response.simulation_shape: linear from 0 at pH 6.0 to 1 at pH 7.0; 1 above 7.0
sources: SRAC 454: 'The optimum pH range for nitrification is 7.0 to 9.0, although most studies indicate that nitrification efficiency is greater at the higher end of this range (high 8s)'
UVI Aquaponic Systems page (via Biofilters corroboration report): nitrification efficient at pH 7.5 and above, practically ceases below 6.0
pH_response.assumption: The linear shape between 6.0 and 7.0 is a modelling assumption; only the endpoints are sourced. The higher efficiency in the high 8s is not modelled (conservative).

evidence_assessment.directness: direct_quote (7.0 optimum, SRAC 454); paraphrase (below 6.0, UVI page via corroboration report)
evidence_assessment.confidence_reason: Two university sources agree on the endpoints. The linear shape between them is an assumption and is low confidence on its own.

temperature_response.optimal_range_source: SRAC 454: 'Biofilters perform optimally at a temperature range of 77 to 86 F' (25 to 30 C)
temperature_response.rate_change_basis: Zhu and Chen 2002, Aquacultural Engineering 26(4):221-237: at 20 C, +4.275 percent per C under TAN-limited conditions (+1.108 percent per C under DO-limited conditions). TAN-limited value used because the simulated system runs in the linear (TAN-limited) regime.
temperature_response.assumption: Applied as a linear decline below 25 C. Zhu and Chen report the effect is weaker than van't Hoff-Arrhenius predicts. No decline above 30 C is modelled (evidence gap).

optimal_range_evidence.confidence_reason: University extension fact sheet; generic biofilter statement, not raft-specific.

rate_change_evidence.confidence_reason: Peer-reviewed study on fixed-film biofilters. Number read from the abstract only; sensitivity was measured at 20 C and extrapolating it linearly is an assumption (low on its own).
rate_change_evidence.cross_check: Losordo et al. 2015 also say temperature effects are less significant than previously thought, consistent with Zhu and Chen.

dissolved_oxygen_response.source: Biofilters corroboration report: 'Nitrifying bacteria become inefficient... below 2 ppm.'
dissolved_oxygen_response.assumption: Linear shape below 2 mg/L is a modelling assumption.

evidence_assessment.confidence_reason: Threshold from university guidance through the Biofilters corroboration report; the linear shape below 2 mg/L is an assumption.

cross_check_areal_rates_g_tan_m2_day.context: nitrifying trickling filter, mean at 27 C, highest hydraulic and TAN load
cross_check_areal_rates_g_tan_m2_day.source: Godoy-Olmos et al. 2019, J. Environ. Chem. Eng. 7(4):103257

evidence_assessment.confidence_reason: Peer-reviewed; trickling filters, marine/temperate RAS context, abstract only. Cross-check only, not used in the model.

cross_check_areal_rates_g_tan_m2_day.context: rotating biological contactors, commercial tilapia RAS, about 28.4 C, pH 7.14
cross_check_areal_rates_g_tan_m2_day.source: Sandu and Hallerman 2013, IntechOpen, doi 10.5772/55841 (values read from a summary of the page, not verbatim; verify)

evidence_assessment.directness: inferred (read from a page summary, not verbatim)
evidence_assessment.confidence_reason: Open-access book chapter; the numbers were not read verbatim. Cross-check only, verify before any use.

records.cross_check_note: At about 30 mg TAN per g feed, the raft equivalence of 180 g feed/m2/day is about 5.4 g TAN/m2 grow area/day. That is far above the per-m2 media rates above, but the raft figure counts all raft-tank surfaces and plant uptake per m2 of grow area, not per m2 of biofilm. The two are not directly comparable; kept as a cross-check only.
gaps: No half-saturation constant for aquaponic raft biofilm.
Organic carbon effect not modelled (Losordo et al. 2015: C:N of 1:1 can cut nitrification by over 70 percent).
Startup ramp still comes from scenario biofilter_maturity, not from a dynamic model.
records.evidence_policy: Trusted Source Map and Source Trust Policy for Aquaponics Layer 1: source levels E5-E0, confidence high/medium/low rule

records.name: Nitrate Sinks: Water Exchange and Calibrated Residual N Loss
records.approval_batch: batch_002: water_exchange approved (C1), residual_loss still candidate (C2)
records.evidence_policy: Trusted Source Map and Source Trust Policy for Aquaponics Layer 1; reliability fields per AGENTS.md 6A
records.equation_text: nitrate_next = nitrate + nitrified - plant_uptake - residual_loss_fraction * nitrified - water_exchange_fraction * nitrate

water_exchange.quote: water (1.5% of system volume daily on average)
water_exchange.source: Rakocy, Bailey, Shultz, Danaher, 'A Commercial-Scale Aquaponic System Developed at the University of the Virgin Islands' (UVI Agricultural Experiment Station; copy hosted at https://www.tag2grow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/UVI-Aquaponics.pdf)
water_exchange.assumption: Make-up water is treated as nitrate-free (source water nitrate unknown; gap). The cause of the 1.5 percent (evaporation, transpiration, sludge and filter-tank discharge) is not stated, so all of it is treated as nitrate-carrying discharge.

review_metadata.source_gate_reason: E4 UVI report by the system's developers, but read from a third-party copy (tag2grow.org), not a UVI-hosted file.
review_metadata.confidence_reason: Direct number from the system developers, averaged over operation. Undated; context partial (cause of the loss not stated).

corroboration.note: SRAC 454: closed systems run 'very little daily water exchange (less than 2 percent)'.

approval.scope: nitrate_sinks.water_exchange 1.5% of system volume per day (C1); residual_loss stays candidate (C2)
approval.record: Approval Batch 002, approved as recommended (thread message 2026-11-26 01:33 Europe/Amsterdam)

residual_loss.mechanism: Denitrification in anaerobic sludge on the filter-tank orchard netting, plus N leaving with clarifier and filter-tank solids. Lumped, because no source gives either rate.
mechanism_quotes: SRAC 454: 'Denitrification occurs in anaerobic pockets that develop in the sludge.'
SRAC 454: 'The frequency of cleaning the netting regulates the degree of denitrification.'
SRAC 454: 'Nitrate-nitrogen levels can be regulated within a range of 1 to 100 milligrams per liter or more.'
UVI report: 'Nitrate levels were controlled by regulating the cleaning frequency of the filter tanks.'
residual_loss.form: fraction of the day's nitrified N lost, because denitrification is driven by the solids (carbon) load, which scales with feed

calibration.method: Solve the steady-state balance at the UVI basil anchor: nitrified = plant uptake + water exchange + residual loss, with nitrate held at the anchor.

anchors.water_volume_basis: UVI report: total system water volume 111,196 L over 214 m2 plant growing area
anchors.plant_uptake: basil shoot N uptake model at the yield anchor (2.0 kg/m2 per 28 days)

calibration.valid_for: UVI-style systems that keep solids on filter-tank netting between weekly cleanings. Not valid for systems that remove all solids or have no anaerobic zones.

cross_check.source: Yang and Kim 2020, 'Comparisons of nitrogen and phosphorus mass balance for tomato-, basil-, and lettuce-based aquaponic and hydroponic systems', Journal of Cleaner Production 274:122619, doi 10.1016/j.jclepro.2020.122619 (abstract via FAO AGRIS)
cross_check.quote: In aquaponics, 59–70% of total N input was estimated to be lost via denitrification (45–50%), wastewater (14–20%), and solid waste (0.7–2%)
cross_check.comparison: The calibrated loss is about 73 percent of nitrified N. If TAN is about 57 percent of feed N (0.092 / 0.16), that is about 42 percent of feed N, close to the 45 to 50 percent denitrification Yang and Kim report. Feed protein at UVI is not in canon, so this is approximate.

review_metadata.source_gate_reason: Mechanism from E4 university sources; the value itself is a calibration, not a measurement.
review_metadata.confidence_reason: Calibrated to one site's nitrate mean, through two other candidate models (TAN placeholder of 30 mg/g feed, basil shoot uptake). Magnitude agrees with an independent peer-reviewed N budget, which lifts it from guess to plausible.

records.sensitivity_note: Gloger et al. 1995 (cited in the UVI report) measured raft removal of 0.83 g total N/m2/day under romaine lettuce, by plant uptake and bacterial oxidation. That is above the basil shoot uptake of about 0.32 g N/m2/day; if real plant uptake is higher, the calibrated residual loss shrinks.
gaps: No measured denitrification rate or sludge N content for UVI.
Source water nitrate unknown; make-up water assumed nitrate-free.
Water exchange does not yet remove TAN, phosphorus or other ions.
